FISHING LICENCE · CANADA

Ontario fishing licence

Anglers aged 18 to 64 need an Outdoors Card and a fishing licence in Ontario. Ontario and Canadian residents under 18 or aged 65 and older fish with government identification instead. Visitors from outside Canada need a licence from age 18, including at 65 and older. A one-day licence does not need an Outdoors Card.

Visitor licence from$15.21 CAD1 calendar day
Buy on the official site ↗Checked against official sources on 26 Nov 2026.

1Who needs a fishing licence in Ontario?

You need a licence

  • Ontario residents and other Canadian residents aged 18 to 64.
  • Visitors from outside Canada aged 18 and older, including those aged 65 and older.

You do not need one

  • Ontario and Canadian residents under 18 or aged 65 and older need no Outdoors Card or licence. They carry government-issued identification that shows their name and date of birth.
  • Visitors from outside Canada under 18 can fish with a licence holder and share that holder's catch limit, or buy their own Outdoors Card and licence for their own limit.
  • Ontario-resident veterans and active Canadian Armed Forces members fish with an NDI 20 or NDI 75 card instead of a licence.
  • Holders of an Ontario accessible parking permit or a CNIB national identity card fish with that document, regardless of residency.
  • Canadian residents could fish without a licence on February 14–16, May 9–10, June 20–21, and June 27–July 5, 2026. Conservation catch limits and all other rules still applied; carry government-issued identification showing your name and date of birth.

3Do you need an extra stamp or permit?

  • Outdoors Card$8.57 CADRequired with every licence except the one-day licence. Valid for 3 calendar years.

4Where can you buy the licence?

Buy online through the Fish and Wildlife Licensing Service with Visa or Mastercard, at a licence issuer, or at a participating ServiceOntario office. Buy the Outdoors Card first, except for a one-day licence. Renew an Outdoors Card and three-year licence by phone at 1-800-288-1155.

Buy on the official site ↗

5Rules to know before you fish

  • Carry your Outdoors Card and licence summary. A digital summary must be the PDF from the licensing service; a photo or screenshot is not valid.
  • Conservation licences have lower catch and possession limits than sport licences.
  • Every licence runs on the calendar year. A one-year licence expires on December 31, whatever the purchase date.
  • A one-day licence is valid for one calendar day and ends at midnight. An eight-day licence covers eight consecutive calendar days.

Questions before your trip

What to confirm before the trip

Listed fees are the official 2026 prices before 13% HST, in effect until December 31, 2026. Confirm zone limits and seasons before the trip.

How much is a fishing licence in Ontario?

For Ontario residents in 2026, a one-year sport fishing licence costs $26.57 CAD and a three-year sport licence costs $79.71. A conservation licence costs $15.07 for one year or $45.21 for three years. A one-day sport licence costs $12.21. Add the Outdoors Card at $8.57, valid for 3 calendar years. All fees are before 13% HST.

Do seniors need a fishing licence in Ontario?

Ontario and Canadian residents aged 65 and older do not need to buy an Outdoors Card or fishing licence. They carry government-issued identification that shows their name and date of birth, and sport licence limits apply. Visitors from outside Canada still need an Outdoors Card and licence at 65 and older.

What age do you need a fishing licence in Ontario?

Ontario and Canadian residents need a licence from age 18 to 64. Residents under 18 fish with government-issued identification. Visitors from outside Canada need a licence from age 18; those under 18 can fish with a licence holder and share that holder's limit, or buy their own licence.

What is the difference between a sport and a conservation fishing licence in Ontario?

A sport fishing licence gives full catch and possession limits. A conservation fishing licence costs less and has reduced catch and possession limits, so it suits anglers who release most fish. The regulations show the two limits as S and C for each species and zone.

How much is a non-resident fishing licence in Ontario?

Canadian residents from outside Ontario pay $55.81 CAD for a one-year sport licence, $33.43 for a one-year conservation licence, or $15.21 for a one-day sport licence. Visitors from outside Canada pay $83.19 for one year sport, $52.71 for one year conservation, $54.38 for an eight-day sport licence, $31.52 for an eight-day conservation licence, or $24.86 for one day. Fees are before 13% HST.

Do I need an Outdoors Card to fish in Ontario?

Yes, with every licence except the one-day sport licence. The Outdoors Card costs $8.57 CAD and is valid for 3 calendar years. Ontario mails the plastic card in about 20 days; until it arrives, carry the licence summary you receive at purchase.

When does an Ontario fishing licence expire?

Ontario issues fishing licences on a calendar year basis, January 1 to December 31. A one-year licence expires on December 31 of the year printed on it, whatever the purchase date. A three-year licence expires on December 31 of its third year.

Can veterans and people with disabilities fish without a licence in Ontario?

Ontario-resident veterans and active Canadian Armed Forces members can fish with an NDI 20 or NDI 75 card instead of a licence. A person with an Ontario accessible parking permit or a CNIB national identity card can fish with that document, regardless of residency. Sport licence limits apply.

When are the free fishing days in Ontario?

Canadian residents could fish without a licence four times in 2026: February 14–16, May 9–10, June 20–21, and June 27–July 5. Conservation licence catch limits apply on those days, and each angler carries government-issued identification with name and date of birth.
